project.title: Every Hurricane Category Explained
project.subtitle: The Deadly Math of Wind, Water, and the Category 6 Debate

scientific_pedagogy.core_thesis: Human perception assumes hurricane categories scale linearly (1 to 5), but dynamic aerodynamic wind pressure scales with the square of velocity (v^2) and kinetic energy dissipation scales with the cube (v^3). Cat 5 delivers 4.5x the dynamic pressure and 20x the destructive potential of Cat 1.

formulas.name: Dynamic Aerodynamic Pressure
formulas.description: Pressure exerted by moving air on a perpendicular surface (rho = 1.225 kg/m^3)

formulas.name: Kinetic Energy Flux / Destructive Power
formulas.description: Rate of kinetic energy delivered per unit time, scaling cubically with wind speed

formulas.name: Bernoulli Lift on Roof Structures
formulas.description: Pressure drop above roof ridge causing vertical uplift and framing shear

formulas.name: Hydrostatic Storm Surge Drag
formulas.description: Wind shear stress piling ocean water against shallow continental shelves

visual_analogies.name: The Inverted Umbrella Wind Tunnel
visual_analogies.mechanic: Magi tests standard umbrella at 75 mph (Cat 1) inside an aeronautical wind tunnel; ribs flex, snap backward, and yank Magi off his feet.

visual_analogies.name: The 3D House Aerodynamic Cross-Section
visual_analogies.mechanic: Windward stagnation pressure pushes inward, accelerating airflow creates negative suction over eaves. Garage door fails, attic pressurizes like a balloon, and roof trusses pop off like a champagne cork.

visual_analogies.name: The Glass Water Tank Flume
visual_analogies.mechanic: Cross-section flume showing seawater (800x denser than air). Surface wind friction rolls water forward; shallow shelf forces water vertically into a 20+ ft surge obliterating coastal models.

visual_analogies.name: The Open-Ended Category 6 Gauge
visual_analogies.mechanic: Saffir-Simpson gauge hits 157 mph peg at Cat 5. Needle breaks the glass dial as sea temperatures exceed 86°F, reaching 192+ mph (Patricia 215 mph, Haiyan 195 mph).

cat_1.structural_damage: Minimal framing damage, loose roof shingles torn, large tree branches snap, power lines downed causing short localized blackouts.

cat_2.structural_damage: Extensive roof and siding damage, shallow-rooted trees uprooted blocking roads, near-total power loss lasting days to weeks.

cat_3.structural_damage: Major hurricane classification. Severe structural framing failure, gable roofs sheared off, municipal water and electricity out for weeks.

cat_4.structural_damage: Catastrophic damage. Complete roof structure detachment, exterior wall collapse on framed homes, most trees snapped, area uninhabitable for months.

cat_5.structural_damage: Total structural obliteration. Wood-framed houses wiped clean to concrete foundation slabs, steel transmission towers bent, industrial envelope failure.

cat_6_proposal.proposed_by: Michael Wehner (LBNL) & James Kossin (First Street Foundation), PNAS 2024
